item.title: Paraguay ex-president Peña placed under house arrest after impeachment
item.description: Paraguayan President Santiago Pena was placed under house arrest on Friday on suspicion of breach of trust, shortly after the Senate removed him from office over the collapse of a major bank tied to his government. Pena had offered his resignation over the disaster, but lawmakers pressed ahead with impeachment proceedings that would strip him of immunity granted to former presidents. He did not attend the trial in the Senate despite earlier pledging to defend himself. The president “is declared... Publicado también por: South China Morning Post. item.title: ¿Regulación o burbuja? Qué hay detrás de la caída de las tecnológicas luego de las midterms en EE. UU.
item.description: La victoria de los demócratas en las elecciones de mitad de mandato en Estados Unidos provocó una ola de ventas en el sector tecnológico, que llevó al Nasdaq a caer más de 5,5% en su peor jornada desde abril de 2025. Los centros de datos, que precisan enormes cantidades de agua y energía, se convirtieron en tema de campaña, pero especialistas consultadas por France 24 dudan de que el nuevo Congreso imponga límites verdaderos al desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Is Israel opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot going to replace Benjamin Netanyahu?
item.description: In Israel, Gadi Eisenkot emerged on Thursday, November 5, as the frontrunner to be tasked with forming a government. This comes after one of the two main parties representing ultra-Orthodox Jewish voters – a longtime ally of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition – declined to recommend any candidate for the task. FRANCE 24's correspondent in Jerusalem Noga Tarnopolsky reports. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro battles to remain relevant as he speaks at rightwing conference at Mar-a-Lago
item.description: Far-right politician addresses Conservative Political Action Conference and makes unsubstantiated claims about election fraud Flávio Bolsonaro, the far-right politician who lost Brazil’s presidential election last month, has insisted his defeat is not “the end for Brazil” as he battles to maintain political relevance after fleeing to the US. Bolsonaro absconded early last week shortly after losing the 25 October election to the leftwing incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva by more than 4m votes. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.
item.dc:creator: Tom Phillips in Rio de Janeiro

item.title: ‘Profound anger’ among black voters over Kemi Badenoch’s slavery remarks
item.description: Operation Black Vote chair says Tory leader’s claim that Britain should not apologise has caused ‘hurt and disbelief’ The Conservative leader, Kemi Badenoch, has caused “profound anger, hurt and disbelief” among many black voters with her comments about transatlantic slavery, according to the chair of Operation Black Vote (OBV), who urged the prime minister, Andy Burnham, to apologise for Britain’s involvement without delay. David Weaver, a former government adviser, said the Labour and Tory leaders risked alienating black voters with their handling of the issue of a state apology for… Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: ANC faces bruising defeat in South African local elections with 80% of ballots counted
item.description: Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80% of ballots counted. Wednesday’s fragmented vote marks another stage in the decline of the ANC, which has led national governments since the end of white minority apartheid rule in 1994. High unemployment, crime, corruption and poor local service delivery have all contributed to… Fuente: The Guardian - World.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg

item.title: 'Period of uncertainty: Trump is tormented, he's unstoppable, and he's desperate for immortality'
item.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Craig Copetas, Greek-American author, international affairs columnist and editor at Türkiye Today and French Senator Hélène Conway-Mouret. “What you have is a tormented and unstable president who's desperate for immortality.” With this arresting assessment, Copetas captures what he considers the defining paradox of Donald Trump's presidency in the aftermath of the US midterm elections: a leader politically neutered at home but potentially emboldened on the international stage. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: François PICARD
